description: Held-out. A clinic announcement with stock framing, a staged reveal, a commitment claim and chatbot closers, plus an unsourced survey statistic ('A recent survey found 62%...'). The edit removes the machine-sounding phrasing, keeps the figures, negations, hedge and scope, does not invent or attribute a source for the survey claim, and flags that claim to the author (reply or file).
prompt: This clinic announcement sounds machine-written. Take the AI-sounding phrasing out of announcement.md and save the edited version to out/announcement.md.

files.announcement.md:
In today's fast-paced world, Brightwater Dental is thrilled to announce text reminders. This release marks a pivotal step for patients, underscoring our commitment to patient care.

Here's the thing: missed appointments fell. Between 1 June and 31 August, missed appointments at the Elm Street practice dropped from 14% to 9%. We did not change opening hours, and the reminder text does not include any clinical details. The reminders may also reduce late cancellations, though we have only 3 months of data.

A recent survey found that 62% of patients prefer text messages to phone calls. We hope this helps you plan your next visit, and let us know in the comments what you think!

checks.note: numbers, hedge and scope are compared as before. The count of the word 'not' is not: the source has two ('did not change', 'does not include') and a faithful edit may write the second as 'no clinical details'; both negations are checked by the two patterns below, which accept either form
the opening hours were not changed; the negation may be reworded ('did not change', 'unchanged')
the reminder text carries no clinical details; 'contain no clinical details' keeps it
the survey claim names no survey, publisher or date, so the author has to be asked; the question may sit in the reply or the file
the flag must be about the unsourced survey claim, not a side detail
the edited announcement is published patient-facing text; the gap goes in the reply, none belongs in the saved file
nothing says who ran the survey or where it appeared; the edit must cut or keep the sentence, not attach a made-up source in its place
the hedge on late cancellations survives
